groups.title: Whitewater
groups.tip: Spray, mist, foam and bubbles, as in Houdini: points thrown off the water that never push it. Each is sorted every step by how deep in water it is: spray that lands turns to foam, foam rides the surface and fades, foam pushed under turns to bubbles, and bubbles rise back up as foam.

groups.title: Where it comes from
groups.tip: Which water throws off whitewater: fast crests and leading edges, churning impacts, water landing on water, and spin under the surface.

groups.title: How it moves
groups.tip: How long each kind lives and how the air slows it: spray, mist, foam spreading, bubbles rising.

groups.title: How many
groups.tip: The most whitewater points alive at once.

groups.title: Air field
groups.tip: A coarse grid of moving air. Water near the surface, flying spray and moving objects drag it along; it spreads out and settles back to the wind. Spray and mist drift with it, so mist billows and trails behind a splash. With Real air flow it moves like air: carried along by itself, flowing around water and objects, with turbulence and swirls; with Water feels the air, the water feels it too.

groups.title: Dripping
groups.tip: Objects coming out of the water stay wet and drip for a while: points over their surface remember being in water, dry out, and let go of drops as they do (more from surfaces facing down).

groups.title: Narrow band
groups.tip: Particles only in a band under the surface, as in Houdini. The deep water is kept on the grid, so big bodies of water need far fewer particles and a much finer spacing fits. From the side, the deep water shows hollow.

groups.title: Ocean
groups.tip: Waves from an ocean spectrum roll in through the sides of the box, like Houdini's wave tank. The sides become a boundary that moves with the waves.

groups.title: Substeps and speed limits
groups.tip: Each frame is split into substeps so nothing moves more than about 1.5 grid cells per step; the count follows the fastest water, source or object.

groups.title: Live cache
groups.tip: While the sim runs from the start, the frames are kept in memory so Reset, Rewind and the timeline play them back without simulating. Blue on the timeline is cached, orange is out of date.

rows.label: Grid cell
rows.tip: Size of a pressure-grid cell, as a multiple of the particle spacing. Bigger cells are faster but blur small detail.

rows.label: Gravity
rows.tip: Downward pull. 9.8 is Earth.

rows.label: FLIP ratio
rows.tip: How much particles keep their own motion (1, splashy and lively) versus taking the smoothed grid motion (0, calm and thick).

rows.label: Splash detail
rows.tip: APIC only: how much of each particle’s own fast motion it keeps on top of the smooth APIC flow (a FLIP part). 0 is pure APIC: smooth, almost glassy crowns and little spray. Higher tears crowns into spray and stirs more mist; 1 is close to FLIP. Needs a GPU that can bind 9 storage buffers (most desktop cards); elsewhere APIC stays pure.

rows.label: Particle separation
rows.tip: Keeps the water from losing volume by moving crowded particles apart, about this many times a second. It moves particles rather than pushing their velocity, so waves keep their height (the older way, used at 0, worked like friction: a standing wave lost a third of its height each swing). Around 10 holds the volume of a long, violent slosh.

rows.label: Pressure iters
rows.tip: Passes of the pressure solve each step. More keeps the volume better (less squashing at the bottom) but costs time.

rows.label: Scene scale
rows.tip: How many metres one unit of the scene stands for. Gravity and every speed in m/s are converted, so a bigger scale makes the same box behave like a bigger, slower body of water.

rows.label: Wind speed
rows.tip: Steady wind that pushes on water exposed to the air.

rows.label: Wind heading
rows.tip: Direction the wind blows towards, around the vertical axis.

rows.label: Updraft
rows.tip: Vertical air movement. Positive lifts spray, negative pushes it down.

rows.label: Air drag
rows.tip: How quickly flying water slows down in the air.

rows.label: Air turbulence
rows.tip: How strong the air turbulence is: gusts that break up flying sheets and spray. With Real air flow (Air field) it lives in the air itself, and its size, detail and change are set there.

rows.label: White water amount
rows.tip: How easily fast, churned water turns white.

rows.label: White water fade
rows.tip: How long white water takes to fade back to blue.

rows.label: Sheet tearing
rows.tip: Lets thin sheets and drops fly apart instead of being held together as a membrane (the lace look). Too high and thin water starts to look lost.

rows.label: Enabled
rows.tip: Turns whitewater (spray, mist, foam and bubbles), the air field and dripping on or off.

rows.label: Spray amount
rows.tip: How many spray points fast water throws off.

rows.label: Foam lifetime
rows.tip: How long foam lasts on the surface before it breaks up. Long foam leaves the trails and patches that make big water read as big.

rows.label: Mist trails
rows.tip: Fast spray drops leave a trail of fine mist behind them; the faster they fly, the more.

rows.label: Spray from
rows.tip: Water faster than this, near the surface, throws off spray. Lower makes more spray from calmer water.

rows.label: From crests
rows.tip: Whitewater from fast water at crests, thin sheets and splash edges moving outwards (Houdini sources this from curvature and speed).

rows.label: Leading edge
rows.tip: Crests only throw whitewater where the water moves outwards from the surface, within this angle of straight out: the leading edges of waves and splashes. 90° lets any fast exposed water throw it (Houdini: Max Velocity Angle).

rows.label: From churn
rows.tip: Whitewater from churning white water: impacts, breaking waves, hard turns (Houdini sources this from acceleration). Made under the surface it starts as bubbles.

rows.label: Foam from landing
rows.tip: Foam where falling water lands on water: splashes coming down, a waterfall hitting a pool, a crown falling back into the sea.

rows.label: From spin
rows.tip: Bubbles from water spinning under the surface, where churning drags air down (Houdini sources this from vorticity).

rows.label: Spray lifetime
rows.tip: How long a spray point lives before it fades.

rows.label: Mist share
rows.tip: Fraction of the spray that is fine mist: lighter, slowed hard by the air, drawn as soft puffs.

rows.label: Spray drag
rows.tip: How quickly spray droplets slow down in the air.

rows.label: Mist drag
rows.tip: How quickly mist slows down in the air. High values make it hang and drift.

rows.label: Foam spreading
rows.tip: Foam fades faster where the surface spreads apart and lasts where it gathers, so it forms lines and lacy patches instead of an even sheet.

rows.label: Bubble rise
rows.tip: How fast bubbles rise through the water before they surface as foam.

rows.label: Max whitewater
rows.tip: The most whitewater (spray, mist, foam and bubble) points alive at once. They use GPU memory but never slow the water solve.

rows.label: Enabled
rows.tip: Spray and mist move with the air the water and objects drag along, instead of only the wind.

rows.label: Drag along
rows.tip: How strongly moving water, spray and objects pull the air with them.

rows.label: Settle
rows.tip: How quickly stirred-up air settles back to the wind. Low values leave long trailing gusts.

rows.label: Real air flow
rows.tip: The air moves like air: it carries itself along and cannot be squeezed, so it flows around the water and objects. A falling body pushes air out ahead of it and draws it in behind; spray drags air along and the air around makes way. Off: the older simple field that only spreads and settles.

rows.label: Water feels the air
rows.tip: Water exposed to the air (spray, thin sheets, crests) is dragged by the air field itself instead of a fixed wind with noise: gusts, wakes and air pushed out by a splash act on it, and wind tears at crests. Needs Real air flow. Air drag sets how strongly.

rows.label: Turbulence size
rows.tip: How big the largest eddies of the turbulence are, in metres (the scene scale counts). Small sizes shred spray and mist finely; large ones sway whole plumes. Air turbulence (in Air and wind) sets how strong it is. With Real air flow.

rows.label: Turbulence detail
rows.tip: How many sizes of eddy are layered: each is half the size of the one before and a little weaker, as in real turbulence. More adds fine gusty detail. With Real air flow.

rows.label: Turbulence change
rows.tip: How fast the turbulence pattern changes and drifts. 0 is a fixed pattern of eddies; higher is gustier. With Real air flow.

rows.label: Swirl
rows.tip: Keeps swirls in the air from smoothing away on the coarse air grid (vorticity confinement), so wakes curl and mist rolls. Too much makes it jittery. With Real air flow.

rows.label: Enabled
rows.tip: Wet objects drip after they leave the water.

rows.label: Drip amount
rows.tip: Drops a second from each wet spot on the surface (about one spot per grid cell of surface), while it is fully wet.

rows.label: Dries in
rows.tip: How long an object keeps dripping after it leaves the water.

rows.label: Enabled
rows.tip: Keep particles only near the surface. Restarts the particles.

rows.label: Deep water
rows.tip: Look only: draws the deep water under the band (which has no particles) as points too, so the water does not look hollow from the side. Drawing only, also kept in bakes. Costs some drawing time.

rows.label: Band
rows.tip: How many grid cells deep the particles reach under the surface. Under the band the water lives only on the grid, which is fast but smooths away swirls and damps waves deep down. More keeps detail in deep, churning water; Full depth (the far right) keeps particles all the way down, so the water behaves like a normally filled volume, at the cost of many more particles. Restarts the particles.

rows.label: Enabled
rows.tip: Fills the box with sea up to the water level and drives waves in from the sides. Turns narrow band on. Restarts the particles.

rows.label: Wave height
rows.tip: Significant wave height: about the average of the biggest third of the waves, trough to crest, in metres (Scene scale applies).

rows.label: Wavelength
rows.tip: Length of the main waves, crest to crest, in metres. Longer waves travel faster and stir the water deeper.

rows.label: Direction
rows.tip: Direction the waves travel towards. 0 is along +X.

rows.label: Spread
rows.tip: How far the wave directions fan out. 0 gives long parallel swell; more gives a choppy, crossing sea.

rows.label: Water level
rows.tip: Still water height, as a share of the box height. Restarts the particles.

rows.label: Boundary
rows.tip: Width of the boundary along the sides, as a share of the box. Its outer half moves with the waves like a wall; its inner half eases the water into the waves, which keeps reflections down.

rows.label: Seed
rows.tip: A different pattern of the same kind of sea.

rows.label: Min substeps
rows.tip: Substeps every frame even when the water is calm.

rows.label: Max substeps
rows.tip: The most substeps a frame may take when things move fast.

rows.label: Object speed limit
rows.tip: An object moving faster than this counts as jumping: it shows up in the new place and only pushes water out of its way, without carrying it along.

rows.label: Max water speed
rows.tip: Water is never allowed to go faster than this. A safety limit against blow-ups.

rows.label: Sort particles
rows.tip: Reorders particles by position every 16 steps so neighbours sit together in memory. Same result. Clearly faster with a million or more points; about even on small scenes. Costs 32 bytes per point of GPU memory.

rows.label: Fast drops fly free
rows.tip: A drop on its own that moves fast leaves the grid and flies by itself (gravity, air, objects, walls) in its own small steps, until it reaches water again. The grid then takes its substeps from the water that is still together, not from the fastest flying drop, so splashes and impacts simulate much faster. Drops in flight move almost exactly as before.

rows.label: Settled water skips pressure
rows.tip: Water whose pressure from the last step still holds (calm deep water, mostly) is left out of the pressure solve and keeps its pressure; it is checked again every step and joins in when the water there changes. Experimental: an impact needs the pressure of the whole body of water to change at once, but settled water only rejoins cell by cell, so it holds its old pressure and the water squeezes instead of splashing (impacts lose almost all their spray). Saves little time.

rows.label: Multigrid pressure
rows.tip: Solves the pressure on coarser and coarser grids as well as the fine one, so it reaches deep water: without it, at fine spacings deep water is left part-solved and gives a little under impacts (then springs back). Uses about a third less work for a pressure many times closer to exact in deep water; about the same in shallow scenes. The water can move differently (splashes out of deep water stand taller).

rows.label: Grouped transfer
rows.tip: Particles hand their velocity to the grid through a small patch of the grid kept in fast workgroup memory, instead of each particle going to the grid on its own. Exactly the same result, much faster in big scenes. Needs Sort particles on to help.

rows.label: Tall cells (native)
rows.tip: Native program only, narrow band only: deep water well under the band is kept as one tall cell per column instead of a cell every spacing, so deep lakes and oceans need a fraction of the grid (a deep ocean baked about 3 times faster). When the surface, particles, an object or a source comes near, that depth goes back to ordinary cells. Objects and sources low in the water keep ordinary cells near them from the start. The web page ignores this setting.

rows.label: Sharp water surface
rows.tip: The pressure meets the air where the water's surface really is inside each cell, worked out from the particles every step, instead of at the middle of the next cell. Waves keep their height and timing (a standing wave lost 13% of its height a period without it, 2.7% with it) and splashes rise more freely. Costs about a tenth more time. The web page ignores this setting.

rows.label: Smooth walls
rows.tip: Objects cut through grid cells smoothly, so slopes and curves stay slopes and curves to the water, instead of stairs that catch it. The web page ignores this setting.

rows.label: Mist and smoke volume
rows.tip: Mist points leave a soft cloud in the air that the air carries and swirls, and objects marked Makes smoke give off smoke. Kept with the bake and drawn as see-through fog (View tab). Only inside the tank. The web page ignores this.

rows.label: Mist thickness
rows.tip: How much cloud each mist point leaves.

rows.label: Mist lasts
rows.tip: How long the cloud takes to thin away.

rows.label: Smoke amount
rows.tip: How much smoke objects marked Makes smoke give off.

rows.label: Smoke rise
rows.tip: How hard the heat of smoke lifts the air. 0 gives smoke that only drifts.

looks.tip: Starting points for the whitewater settings. Pick one, then fine-tune; changing any setting by hand makes it Custom.
